name: Baal Peor
overview: Baal Peor was an idol worshiped by the Moabites that led Israel into grievous sin and provoked the righteous anger of the LORD, as seen when Israel joined themselves to Baal Peor and faced divine judgment (Numbers 25:3, Deuteronomy 4:3). The severity of their idolatry is underscored by Moses' command to execute those who participated in this unfaithfulness (Numbers 25:5). Scripture also highlights the spiritual defilement involved, noting that Israel partook in the sacrifices of the dead associated with Baal Peor (Psalms 106:28), and that their turning to this idol was an act of shame and abomination, reflecting their love for sin (Hosea 9:10).
